name: submit_shader
description:
Submit a shader generation job to the backend. Returns a jobId immediately; the actual GLSL generation runs server-side. Use the track_progress tool with the returned jobId to wait on or inspect the job.

This tool only submits — it does NOT apply the shader to any clip. Applying is a separate edit_item call that the agent does after the user explicitly asks.

See the shader-gen skill (loaded by Skill builtin) for full prompting / type-routing guidance.

name.description: Asset name shown in the library. Defaults to a name derived from the prompt.

prompt.description: Natural-language description of the shader. Restate the user's intent in one concrete sentence — e.g. "Chromatic aberration with RGB split", "Cinematic teal-orange color grade", "Smooth crossfade with soft edge".

referenceAssetIds.description: Project asset ids the generator should learn from. Image asset id → model LOOKS AT it as visual inspiration (e.g. a still to match for a LUT, a screenshot to mimic for a glitch effect). Effect or transition asset id → backend fetches its code and reuses its style. At most one effect/transition reference per submit, and its kind must match `type`. Pass full UUIDs or short id prefixes.

type.description: Whether the shader is a per-clip effect (color, blur, mask, LUT-style grade, distortion) or a between-clip transition (crossfade, wipe, slide, 3D cube). See the shader-gen skill for the full routing table.
